LESSON: READING 6.2.1 INTENSIVE READING COMPREHENSION DIALOGUES

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we guess the meaning of words?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words from a text
2. respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 6.2.1 INTENSIVE READING COMPREHENSION DIALOGUES
This lesson teaches Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues for Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words from a text
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues above.
2. Explain Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues important for a Grade 5 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we guess the meaning of words?
2. What makes you a good reader?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words from a text
2. respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
